title: Balsamic-Mustard Pork Medallions with Asparagus and Couscous
intro: Building a pan sauce from tangy mustard and balsamic vinegar gives this skillet dinner deep flavor without excess saturated fat. Slicing a lean pork tenderloin into quick-cooking medallions keeps the meat tender and speeds up weeknight prep.

ingredients.name: Pork tenderloin
ingredients.canonical_name: Pork, fresh, loin, tenderloin, separable lean only, raw

ingredients.name: Asparagus
ingredients.preparation: tough ends snapped off, cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.name: Low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.canonical_name: Soup, chicken broth, low sodium, canned

instructions: Combine the dry couscous and boiling water in a heatproof bowl. Cover tightly and set aside to steam.
Season the pork medallions evenly with the garlic powder, dried thyme, and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned pork and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, flipping halfway, before transferring to a plate.
Place the asparagus pieces into the same skillet over medium heat. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, tossing occasionally, until tender-crisp, then transfer to the plate with the pork.
Lower the heat to medium-low and whisk the chicken broth, balsamic vinegar, and Dijon mustard into the skillet, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Simmer the liquid for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened into a pan sauce. Return the pork and asparagus to the skillet, turning them to coat evenly.
Fluff the steeped couscous with a fork and divide it between plates. Top with the glazed pork, asparagus, and any remaining pan sauce.
variation: Swap the asparagus for fresh green beans.
conservation: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently on the stovetop.
